subject: problem with multivariate normal for hierarchical model

messages.author: ba47d4626a81b156
messages.subject: problem with multivariate normal for hierarchical model
parts:
Dear Stan users, 

I was trying to run the following model (BPi and log(sigma_epsilon^2) are what I have in the dataset): 

But I have some problem writing the multivariate model for the second part. 


I tried to make a new vector called y_{i} and make y_{i} follow multivariate model. But it doesn't seem to work. (I got the error: Size of random variable (51) and rows of covariance parameter (2) must match in size)


Here is my code: 


data {   
    int<lower=0> n;          // number of subjects
    real<lower=0> BP[n];    // BP 
    row_vector<lower=0>[n] logVarSE; //log (estimated SE^2)
}

parameters {
  real<lower=0> mu;
  real beta0;
  real beta1;
  row_vector<lower=0>[n] theta;    // true BP 
  row_vector<lower=0>[n] sigmaepsilon2;
  cov_matrix[2] Sigma;
}

transformed parameters{

}

model {
        matrix[2,n] Y ;
        row_vector[n] Mu_v;
        matrix[2,n] MU; 
        row_vector<lower=0>[n]logsigmaepsilon2;

        for (i in 1:n){
           logsigmaepsilon2<-log(sigmaepsilon2);
           Y<-append_row(theta,logsigmaepsilon2);
           Mu[i]<-mu;
           MU<-append_row(Mu_v,beta0+beta1*logVarSE);
        }
        
        for (j in 1:n){
        BP[j] ~ normal(theta[j], sqrt(sigmaepsilon2[j]));
        Y[j] ~ multi_normal(MU[j],Sigma);
        }
 }


Any advice is much appreciated! 


Thanks,

Chubing

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] problem with multivariate normal for hierarchical model
parts:
For your proposed model
I don't see how you're going to fit a different theta[i], and 
sigma_epsilon[i] for each observation BP[i].  Shouldn't sigma_epsilon
be a scalar instead of a vector?  In which case, the multivariate 
sampling no longer makes sense.  

Also, if BP is constrained to be positive, normal is probably not
the right distribution.

- Bob

Thanks Bob! 

In my model, theta[i] is the "true" BP[i], and sigma_epsilon[i] is the measurement error of subject i. That's why each observation BP[i] has a different theta[i], and 
sigma_epsilon[i]. 

I think sigma_epsilon is a vector = (sigma_epsilon1,..., sigma_epsilonn). eg: sigma_espilon is the measurement error of subject 1. 

I want for every subject the true BP(theta[i]) and measurement error(sigma_epsilon[i]) follow a multivariate normal model. Does this make sense to you? 

Also, I'll try other distributions for BP.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] problem with multivariate normal for hierarchical model
parts:
I don't think that's going to work because you're trying to
fit a location theta[i] and a scale sigma_epsilon[i]
with only the single observation BP[i].

I think you need to fit the measurement error as something like this:

BP[i] ~ normal(theta[i], sigma_BP);

where there is only a single scalar parameter sigma_BP for the
measurement errors.

Then, you can define a derived quantity for the error if you need
it, or put it in generated quantities or just calculate it on the
outside:

transformed parameters {
vector[I] err;
err <- theta - BP;
}

There's a chapter in the manual on coding measurement error models.

- Bob
